risk_results.risk: Delivery Hero bridge facility discloses a covenant threshold with <10% post-draw headroom, or a covenant breach/waiver is disclosed within 4 quarters of the draw

learning.rule_for_future: When a Watchlist thesis's killer risk is tied to a dated future financing event (a bridge draw, a covenant test), track the ACTUAL disclosed covenant package as it is filed (here, the 2026-08-06 Term Loan Credit Agreement) rather than waiting only for the final acquisition close -- interim financing filings can pre-disclose covenant terms well before the risk fully resolves.
learning.future_research_check: Before the 90d review, pull the primary SEC 8-K/10-Q covenant schedule to compute actual interest-coverage headroom against the disclosed 3.00x minimum, and confirm whether this is Uber's first-ever maintenance covenant or consistent with prior facilities.

pre_mortem_check.notes: thesis_status is on-track with nothing in risk_results resolved either way at 30 days -- the pre-mortem's named killer risk (Delivery Hero bridge drawn without adequate covenant headroom) has a first partial data point (a disclosed 3.00x minimum interest-coverage covenant) but headroom itself remains uncalculated, so this cannot yet be vindicated or contradicted.

memo_delta.summary: Thirty days into the Watchlist call, UBER is up +11.1% (vs. the S&P 500's roughly flat +0.1%), but none of the five forecast-ledger items has resolved and the Critical serial-acquirer/leverage red flag (RF-CAP-004) underlying the Watchlist cap remains open. The one genuinely new fact is the 2026-08-06 Term Loan Credit Agreement, which for the first time discloses part of the Delivery Hero financing package's actual covenant terms (a 3.00x minimum interest-coverage maintenance covenant) -- directly on-point for the thesis's own killer risk, though headroom against that covenant cannot yet be computed.
memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Uber is up about 11% since our August 6 Watchlist call, well ahead of a roughly flat S&P 500, but nothing in the actual thesis has been tested yet. The Delivery Hero acquisition -- the deal whose debt-funded structure is the reason we capped this at Watchlist -- is still on track for a second-half-2027 close, with a shareholder acceptance window running through early November. The one real new piece of information is that Uber has now signed a term loan agreement that, for the first time, discloses an actual financial covenant (a minimum interest-coverage ratio the company has to keep meeting) tied to part of this financing. That is exactly the kind of disclosure our balance-sheet risk was waiting on, but we still cannot calculate how much cushion there actually is. We are not changing the rating. The next real tests are the October 25-November 5 earnings print and the acceptance period's outcome around the same time.
